messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Hospital Course Summary

Patient: [Name]

Admission Date: [Date]

Discharge Date: [Date]
Admission Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

The patient was admitted to our clinic with chronic diarrhea and intermittent abdominal pain. Upon physical examination and review of medical history, a history of gastrointestinal hemorrhage due to peptic ulcer was noted. Abnormal laboratory findings were also identified, including elevated white blood cell count, C-reactive protein, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Additionally, during the colonoscopy, colitis was detected in the biopsy. Imaging, including ultrasonography and CT, revealed inflammation of intestinal loops, the presence of omental inflammatory thickening, and a fluid collection in the pericaecal area. 

Given these findings, the patient was hydrated and prescribed empiric cefixime and metronidazole for treatment. Pain was reduced following drainage of purulent fluid, antibiotics and hydration, and laboratory values returned to within normal limits. The patient was discharged from the hospital and scheduled for elective appendectomy six weeks later.

Discharge Instructions:

The patient is advised to continue the prescribed antibiotics and to carefully follow the instructions provided upon discharge. The patient should also seek medical attention if symptoms recur or worsen. It is important for the patient to avoid potentially harmful foods and drinks, and to follow a healthy and balanced diet while receiving ongoing treatment. Follow-up appointments are scheduled to monitor the patient's condition and progress, and to determine the ongoing course of treatment as necessary.

Signed by: [Name of responsible medical professional]

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for this admission is a pericaecal (appendiceal) abscess from complicated appendicitis: there was a purulent periappendiceal fluid collection, it was treated with drainage and antibiotics, and an interval appendectomy is planned. This is a digestive system disease, chapter K. Acute appendicitis with a localised abscess falls under category K35.

CODE: K35
